recipes.name: Roasted Beet and Potato Soup
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Place potatoes and beets in a baking dish; drizzle with 1 tablespoon olive oil and season with salt and black pepper.
Roast in the preheated oven until tender, about 1 hour. Set aside to cool.

Heat remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add onion, celery, and garlic; cook and stir until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in roasted potatoes and beets, chicken broth, bay leaf, and thyme; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; simmer until celery is very tender, about 45 minutes.
Off heat, discard bay leaf; purée with an immersion blender until smooth. Stir in milk and lemon juice.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Beet and Potato Soup
raw_recipe.description: This creamy roasted beet and potato soup recipe is rich in flavor from roasting the potatoes and beets and is thickened by blending with an immersion blender.

review.reviewBody: Mmmmm!!!! This beautiful megenta color soup is so tasty and delicious!!!! I modified it a bit - I skipped the roasting part (and skipped peeling the red skinned potatoes) and just sauted all the chopped vegetables in a large soup pot. I omitted the thyme - (i dont like it) and instead, after i pureed the soup i added freshly chopped dill. I used soy milk instead of milk. i was a but skeptical about the milk and lemon juice, so i tried the soup before i added those ingredients, then added them and it really balanced the sweetness of the beets. I am glad i added them.

My wife loves beets, so I tried this for her. She really liked it, and even though I'm not necessarily a beet enthusiast myself, I thought it was pretty good. 
I think I roasted the beets and potatoes too long, because they came out kinda dried up and small, but there was definitely a delicious roasted flavor in there at the end, so it didn't hurt it.
Did it with whole milk this time, but will try 1 or 2% next time, and see if it makes a difference.
Also, we don't have an immersible/wand/stick blender, so I just let it cool down, poured it all into our Ninja mixer, added the milk and lemon juice, and that worked just fine - lovely puree. Just had to heat it back up, via the microwave.

Yum! I had a ton of those preroasted Love Beets and needed to get through them quick, so I threw those in the pot instead of making them from scratch. I should have reserved one for the end just to punch up the color. I also added carrot to the vegetables, went heavy on the garlic, and added a pinch of cumin, paprika and curry powder since it was a little too simple at the end. I finished with coconut milk and lemon zest in addition to the juice, then topped with fresh sourdough croutons made with rosemary and garlic. A teaspoon of Ginger Goat hot sauce rounded things off nicely! I like that the recipe is modification friendly!

I had new potatoes, beets and leeks that needed to be used from a farmer's market. I roasted the potatoes diced, with skin on and roasted the beets, diced but unpeeled. I don't think this changed the recipe other than making it easier than it already is. I added leeks to the celery onion sauté and added a lot more garlic, plus more salt and pepper. I used 2% milk to cut down on fat. I thought the flavors blended well together. This soup makes a very good healthy addition to a meal.

Super yummy. I veganized it really simply by switching the chicken stock to veggie, and the milk to cashew cream. I mashed it with a potato masher bc cleaning my immersion blender is a pain. Love it! My husband asked me to make it again!

Want to add more beets to my diet. This recipe was a hit, especially for a cold winter evening. I used sweet potatoes (what I had and offers more nutrients), didn’t purée for a chunkier soup, and I added a dollop of sour cream. A keeper recipe!

Very tasty! Even our non-beet-lovers enjoyed this soup. It's got a hearty but not overly-strong flavor.
I used a can of coconut milk instead of the cream, because that's what I had. 
I will definitely make this again!

I was looking for a recipe that used jarred beets since I had a jar that has been in the cabinet for quite a while and I did not want them to go to waste. As it turned out, I also had 2 large leftover baked potatoes in the fridge which I used with the jarred beets. I thought to myself, what do I have to loose, take the potato from the skins, use the whole jar of beets, juice and all and I am very glad I did. The result was a delicious soup. My husband and I both loved it. 

My intention is to have the soup again for dinner and accompany it with the leftover baked potato skins which I will fill with bacon and cheese and greek yogurt. .

By the way, I also used onion powder (a good heaping tablespoon) since I did not have any onions in the house. Used the last one yesterday and did not want to go to the store on what I figured would be a busy Sunday. Still the soup was yummy!

Really delicious! This didn't taste heavily of beets to me, but nice, balanced, creamy and lightly sweet. I added 4 cloves of garlic instead of one, and used 1/2 cup of half-and-half instead of 1 1/2 of whole milk to keep the soup thicker but still creamy. Delicious and cheap. I will make this again!

Have to say, I hate it when someone rates the recipe after altering it but here I go (was trying to use up leftover misc things in my fridge from Christmas). First off, I used an acorn squash in add'n to the potato and beets (roasted as directed). I used leeks instead of the onion. For the chick broth, I used 1 cup chick broth (all that I had left), 2 cups vegetable broth and 1 cup white wine (btw-"Better than Bouillon" is awesome). For the milk, I used 1 cup hvy cream and 1/2 cup 1% milk (what I had on hand). This was EXCELLENT but rich. Will make again :)
Doubled the veggies, and added garlic and carrots to the roasting pan. Put a pint of heavy cream in the end to finish too. Yummy!!!
I'm not normally a fan of beets but I followed this recipe with beets from our garden. So delicious! I will be making again.
I liked it because I love all the ingredients and they each bring out the flavors of the others. I'm very slow at doing things so it took me extra time but it's simple enough that I didn't mind.

I loved this soup! I followed the recipe pretty closely but I didn't measure the beets and potatoes -- I just used all the beets in a bunch and about the same amount of taters, and it was probably more than the amount called for. I roasted them on day 1 and made the soup on day 2. My beets were golden and the soup was a beautiful bright yellow. The flavor was very beet-y; if you love beets, like I do, you will love this soup. Family liked it as well. But if you don't care for beets, then it's probably not for you.

I made it last week and it was a huge success not only with me but with my whole family. The taste and colour are so appetizing and delicious. It goes well bread on top or on the side.
It is definitely now favourite dish and a staple for me.
Absolutely delicious and simple to make. The fact that my husband had two bowls is a compliment in itself.

What a wonderful soup! I followed the recipe to the letter with no changes and now I just can't stop eating/drinking it. Will make often through the winter. Love the color too. I will probably double or triple the recipe so there's more to savor for longer. Judi D.
I really wanted to like it, but I don't. I followed the recipe exactly. Thanks, anyway.

Awesome soup, beautiful to look at, nice to eat, even cold. I brought with for lunch on the go, but had no place to warm it up, and it wasn't in a thermos. but still good, with a dollop of Greek yogurt and a mini bagel for a side. Made it just as directed.

I followed the recipe and was pleased with the taste and presentation. One mistake I made is that I roasted for the stated time in my convection oven and they were a little over done. My fault. I usually reduce the time accordingly but omitted to do that this time. This is a delightful soup I will make many times in the future. Hubby loved it.
